concept.title: Example: ditaval flagging with outputclass
concept.shortdesc: Rather than using the separate attributes of prop to define flagging details, you can specify outputclass and define the styling and behavior details in the delivery system, such as an HTML web site.

conbody.p: In DITA, the outputclass attribute can be specified on elements to specify hints for how to process or render the elements, such as by using the value of outputclass as the value of HTML class attributes in generated HTML, where it can be used with normal HTML styling mechanisms, such as CSS style sheets.

You can use this same technique for flagging content by setting outputclass on prop elements with an action value of flag. Elements to which the flagging condition applies should then reflect the outputclass value in generated output, i.e., by setting it on HTML class attributes.

This use of outputclass for flagging allows you to define the details of how flagged content is styled in the delivery system, rather than in the DITAVAL file. For example, for web delivery, this allows you to manage the flagging styling in the same CSS style sheets that style the base content. It also means that you can change the styling details without having to update the DITAVAL files and republish the content.

For example, in your published content you want to flag paragraphs for specific audiences with different visual treatments, including adding icons and making expert-level content collapsed by default. To enable this, you use outputclass values of the form flag-audience, which will then allow styling using normal CSS techniques. You also configure the HTML generation processor to wrap expert-level content in HTML details elements to make them inherently collapsible and expandable.

The DITAVAL defines a prop element for each audience value. Each prop element sets the outputclass value to reflect the audience value: <val> <prop att="audience" action="flag" val="novice" outputclass="flag-novice" /> <prop att="audience" action="flag" val="adept" outputclass="flag-adept" /> <prop att="audience" action="flag" val="expert" outputclass="flag-expert" /> </val>

When rendered to HTML, the pargraphs should reflect the outputclass values: ... ...

Novice-level content

Adept-level content

Expand for expert content

Expert-level content

...

The rendered HTML using this style sheet is: An HTML page with four paragraphs, one with unflagged content that is unstyled, the others showing distinct icons, one for each audience value. The expert content is collapsed.
